title: Additional public health indicators for tracking health outcomes and system pressures
asked: Mr Pritam Singh asked what additional public health indicators MOH will publish on a monthly or bi-weekly basis, beyond bed occupancy rates, ward admission waiting times and emergency department attendances, to help the public track health outcomes and system pressures amid Singapore’s transition to a super-aged society.
response: Ms Rahayu Mahzam said MOH already publishes a range of public health indicators: capacity indicators on its website, the annual National Population Health Survey, the National Nutritional Survey, the annual MOH Revenue and Expenditure Estimates (Budget Book) with KPIs such as life expectancy and disease prevalence, and annual National Registry of Disease Office indicators on cancer, chronic kidney failure, stroke and heart attack. She said health outcomes take time to shape and evolve, so fortnightly or monthly reporting would not be appropriate. She added that MOH is reviewing a meaningful way to put out this information and will continue to review the matter.
